content: Floating-point non-associativity ((a+b)+c != a+(b+c) in finite precision) combined with GPU-parallel non-deterministic reduction/accumulation order means bit-exact output cannot be assumed even on the same hardware across runs, and definitely not guaranteed across vendors/drivers. This is well-documented in verifiable-ML-inference literature (optimistic verification via tolerance windows, redundant computation with statistical comparison) and applies equally to GPU rasterization/rendering. Exact-hash verification is only safe for render jobs with a numerically-simple, deterministic pipeline (e.g. flat-shaded/unlit single-mesh raster with no floating-point-order-sensitive blending); anything more complex needs tolerance-based or redundancy-based verification akin to Golem's perceptual-similarity approach for Blender rendering.
